title: Potato Salad with Egg, Made with Mayonnaise

content.title: About
content.content: Potato salad with boiled potatoes, boiled eggs and mayonnaise is a classic Russian dish often served at celebrations and picnics. The potatoes and eggs provide heartiness, while the mayonnaise gives a smooth, creamy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad became popular in the Soviet era as a quick dish made from readily available ingredients.
In different regions people add mustard, green onion or dill for extra flavor.
Traditionally the salad is served chilled, but in hot weather it is kept in the fridge until serving.
A common variation includes boiled carrots and peas, making the dish more colorful.
Homemade Soviet‑era mayonnaise was often made from eggs, vegetable oil and vinegar.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Eggs and potatoes provide complete proteins essential for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs are rich in vitamin B12, while potatoes supply vitamin B6, both important for metabolism.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes contain potassium, which supports normal heart and muscle function.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Eggs contribute a modest amount of iron, necessary for blood formation.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from potatoes and fats from mayonnaise provides lasting satiety.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Mayonnaise makes the dish calorie‑dense; people watching their weight should control portions.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: The salad should be refrigerated and consumed within 2‑3 days to prevent bacterial growth.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs may experience reactions after eating the salad.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol, so those with high cholesterol should eat the salad in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a starter or side dish. Garnish with fresh herbs, cucumber slices or tomato wedges. It pairs well with meat appetizers, sausage or fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Consume within 2‑3 days. Discard if it develops an off smell or color change.
